clue.text: Batting referred to was encouraging

parts.note: a batsman who is batting is in
cited means referred to or quoted

explanation.surface: A cricket report says the innings mentioned was a promising one.
explanation.definitionFit: To incite is to urge or spur someone on, so the past tense matches a stirring-up that already happened.

clue.text: Effect produced by one law MP introduced

indicators.note: introduced says the MP is put inside the other pieces, as a bill is brought into parliament

parts.note: the Roman numeral I is one
an act is a law passed by parliament
taken as written: Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: A new statute brought in by a member of parliament has consequences.
explanation.walkthrough: IACT opens up to admit MP.
explanation.definitionFit: An impact is the strong effect or influence something has.

clue.text: Greek islander takes up Italian wine

parts.note: a Chian is a native of Chios, a Greek island

indicators.note: takes up in a down clue means the following word is lifted and read upwards

parts.note: It is short for Italian, as in It vermouth

explanation.surface: A man from a Greek island starts drinking a red from Tuscany.
explanation.walkthrough: IT read upwards gives TI.
explanation.definitionFit: This red is made in the Tuscan hills, a famous example of Italian vino.

clue.text: Inaction's odd for a conductor

indicators.note: odd tells us the letters of inaction's are arranged in a strange new way

explanation.surface: A remark that idleness seems strange for a man who leads an orchestra.
explanation.definitionFit: Arturo Toscanini was a celebrated Italian maestro who led orchestras.

clue.text: Such a fearless person could be darned tough

indicators.note: could be suggests the letters of darned tough may be turned into something else

explanation.surface: A brave soul is described as extremely hardy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'could be' tells us to rearrange DARNEDTOUGH.
explanation.definitionFit: Literally one who dreads nothing; the word is also a battleship class named for that boldness.

clue.text: Conceited type, unlike Goldsmith's village parson

explanation.surface: A vain person is contrasted with a humble churchman from an eighteenth-century poem.
explanation.walkthrough: Goldsmith's poem The Deserted Village marvels 'that one small head could carry all he knew' of its village schoolmaster; a man with a small head is the opposite of the vain type.
explanation.definitionFit: An arrogant, self-important person is colloquially said to have a swollen head; the poem's figure, by contrast, has a small one.

clue.text: Old plane in America carrying 5 ac

indicators.note: carrying in a down clue puts the America piece below, bearing the other on top

parts.note: 5 across is BIG HEAD, read as the head of the word big, its first letter
US is short for the United States

explanation.surface: A vintage aircraft in the States holds an arrogant passenger.
explanation.walkthrough: 5 across reads as 'big head', the head of 'big'; that is B, sitting on US.
explanation.definitionFit: Bus is airman's slang for an aircraft, especially an old or ungainly one.

clue.text: Children between March and July, for example

definitions.text: Children between March and July, for example

parts.words: Children between March and July, for example
parts.note: the months between March and July are April, May and June, which are all female first names

explanation.surface: Kids born in spring are being described.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests children born in spring; really April, May and June are girls' names.
explanation.definitionFit: Young females are a kind of children, and three months are their names.

clue.text: Resilient enough to survive in broken ice

indicators.note: in tells us the word for survive sits within the broken ice
broken says the letters of ice are shattered into a new order

parts.note: to last is to survive or endure

explanation.surface: Something tough enough to last when ice cracks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broken' rearranges ICE into EIC, which then holds LAST.
explanation.definitionFit: Something springy that returns to its shape is flexible and resilient.

clue.text: A remarkable sea upset rum

indicators.note: upset in a down clue means the pieces are turned upside down, read from the bottom

parts.note: rare means unusual, remarkable
the Med is the Mediterranean Sea

explanation.surface: An extraordinary stretch of water spills a sailor's drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rum' looks like the adjective 'odd' but is the drink; 'upset' turns A RARE MED upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: This rum takes its name from a district of Guyana, which also gives its name to brown sugar.

clue.text: Hero, say, meddles with a pure woman

parts.note: one who pries meddles or snoops
Tess of the d'Urbervilles bears the subtitle A Pure Woman, so the phrase names Hardy's heroine Tess

explanation.surface: A heroic man is said to interfere with a virtuous lady.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hero' looks like a brave man, but in Greek legend Hero, beloved of Leander, served Aphrodite at Sestos in a sacred office.
explanation.definitionFit: In myth Hero held a religious office in a temple of Aphrodite, an example of a female cleric of the old gods.

clue.text: Improve weapons to raise morale, initially

parts.note: to rear is to raise, as children or animals

indicators.note: initially asks for only the opening letter of the word morale

explanation.surface: Better arms are proposed as a way to lift the troops' spirits.
explanation.definitionFit: To equip an army afresh with weapons is to restore or upgrade its armament.

clue.text: A number of Cubans taking steps to follow leader

definitions.text: A number of Cubans taking steps to follow leader

parts.words: A number of Cubans taking steps to follow leader
parts.note: a Latin American dance where people form a line behind a leader; 'number' is a musical piece, not a count

explanation.surface: A group of people from Cuba fall in line behind someone in charge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A number of Cubans' looks like a crowd; a number is also a song or dance, and this one is Cuban, danced in a snaking line copying the person in front.
explanation.definitionFit: This Cuban dance has dancers step in single file behind a leader, kicking in time.

clue.text: In Dorset I upset river bank user

indicators.note: In tells us the river goes inside the jumbled letters of Dorset I
upset says the letters of Dorset I are knocked into a new order

parts.note: the Po is the great river of northern Italy

explanation.surface: Someone in a southern English county is annoyed by a man fishing from the riverside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'river bank user' reads like an angler; the bank is a money bank. DESITOR, rearranged from Dorset I, takes PO inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who places money with a bank for safekeeping is its customer, using it to hold funds.

clue.text: Arguments between publicity men and criminals

parts.note: PROs are public relations officers, publicity men
cons are convicts, criminals

explanation.surface: Debates rage between spin doctors and crooks.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase sums up the reasons for and against, the points of a debate.

clue.text: Man in charge of military affairs

definitions.text: Man in charge of military affairs

parts.words: Man in charge of military affairs
parts.note: affairs read as romances suggests a soldier with love interests; really it is the officer who handles contact and cooperation between units

explanation.surface: A commander directs the business of the armed forces.
explanation.walkthrough: The second sense of 'affairs' as liaisons makes the joke: the officer handles links between forces, not love affairs.
explanation.definitionFit: This officer is responsible for communication and coordination between military units or allied forces.

clue.text: False, this? Possibly

indicators.note: Possibly hints that the letters of false and this might be rearranged

explanation.surface: A question whether this statement is untrue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Possibly' signals rearranging FALSETHIS, and the whole clue also defines the result.
explanation.definitionFit: A disloyal or untrue person is unfaithful, false to promises.

clue.text: Renounce, taking a second to diminish gradually

parts.note: s is the standard abbreviation for second, a unit of time
to wear off is to fade away gradually

explanation.surface: Someone gives up something slowly, taking a brief moment.
explanation.definitionFit: To forswear a habit, such as drinking, is to give it up by vow.

clue.text: Current assets in busy City

parts.note: someone working is busy at a task
a capital is a country's chief city

explanation.surface: A financial report lists the holdings of a firm in a bustling metropolis.
explanation.definitionFit: In accounting, this term means a firm's short-term funds, its current assets less liabilities.

clue.text: Drummer to originate repetition of theme

parts.note: drummer is old American slang for a travelling salesman, a rep
to rise is to originate, as a river rises from its source

explanation.surface: A percussionist begins playing a recurring musical motif.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drummer' looks like a percussionist, but in old US slang a drummer is a salesman drumming up trade.
explanation.definitionFit: In music a reprise is a return of an earlier passage or tune.

clue.text: Female imposing on a city in US

indicators.note: on in a down clue puts the imposing piece above the a

parts.note: august means imposing, venerable

explanation.surface: A woman lords it over an American city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Female' adds that Augusta is also a woman's name; the city is the capital of Maine, and another lies in Georgia.
explanation.definitionFit: Augusta is the capital of Maine and also a Georgia city famed for golf.

clue.text: Expense, so to speak, in old money

definitions.text: Expense, so to speak, in old money

parts.words: Expense, so to speak, in old money
parts.note: a cost expressed in pre-decimal British coinage, where a two-shilling piece was a common sum

explanation.surface: A cost is given in pre-decimal currency.
explanation.walkthrough: Before 1971 Britain used pounds, shillings and pence; the coin meant here was worth two shillings.
explanation.definitionFit: This former British two-shilling coin was one unit in which a sum could be paid.

clue.text: Fixed sharp on a piano

indicators.note: on in an across clue places the sharp piece after the letters it sits beside

parts.note: p is the musical abbreviation for piano, meaning softly
a sharp edge or tip is pointed

explanation.surface: A musical note is corrected by playing a sharp on the keyboard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sharp' and 'piano' suggest music, but 'sharp' is POINTED and piano is just P.
explanation.definitionFit: Something fixed, as a time or date, has been set or arranged in advance.

clue.text: Awkward female bird held up by it

indicators.note: by here means held by, so the bird sits within the letters of it
held up in a down clue means the bird is lifted and read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: a pen is a female swan

explanation.surface: A clumsy hen is carried aloft by something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Awkward' tempts as an anagram signal but is the definition; the female bird is a swan, not a hen.
explanation.definitionFit: Clumsy and lacking skill, an inept person is ungainly.

clue.text: Philosopher he turned on

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: turned means the word for on is read backwards

parts.note: in cricket the on side is also called the leg side

explanation.surface: A thinker is said to have rounded on someone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned' reverses LEG to give GEL. The cricket on side is also the leg side.
explanation.definitionFit: Hegel was a German idealist thinker known for his dialectical method.

clue.text: United about small change, I suppose

indicators.note: about tells us the word for united goes round the other pieces

parts.note: things united are made one
p, a penny, is small change in British money

explanation.surface: Someone guesses that a single coin has been placed around.
explanation.definitionFit: To venture a view or hold an opinion is to suppose something.

clue.text: Higgins, for example, in the-chair

explanation.surface: Shaw's phonetics expert is presiding at a meeting.
explanation.walkthrough: Henry Higgins teaches Eliza in Shaw's Pygmalion; a university chair is a senior academic post, so its holder sits 'in the chair'.
explanation.definitionFit: Higgins is a senior academic in the play, and such a scholar holds a university chair.

clue.text: Foot put on pitch

explanation.surface: A footballer is sent out onto the field.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Foot' is to foot the bill; in sailing, to pay a seam is to coat it with pitch to seal it.
explanation.definitionFit: To foot a bill is to settle it; sailors also used the word for smearing tar on a hull.

clue.text: Run round old court at speed

indicators.note: round tells us the word for run goes about the court

parts.note: to fly is to run off quickly
a court leet was a manorial court of medieval England

explanation.surface: Someone jogs a lap of a historic courtyard quickly.
explanation.walkthrough: A court leet was a local lord's court in medieval England.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something with swiftness, as a fast runner does, is moving quickly.

clue.text: Units, as ordered, keep going

indicators.note: as ordered tells us the letters of units and as are rearranged

explanation.surface: Soldiers are told to carry on as commanded.
explanation.walkthrough: 'as ordered' sounds military; it signals rearranging UNITSAS.
explanation.definitionFit: To maintain or prolong an effort is to keep it up.
